clarified_description: Add a thin 'signed-in' strip to the top of the Northline Bank sandbox site's header that reads "Signed in as Alex Taylor". The site has no authentication and deliberately behaves as if the fictional customer Alex Taylor is always signed in (lib/accounts.ts); the strip makes that visible the way real internet banking does. The strip is rendered inside the existing site header (components/Header.tsx, the page's single banner landmark), above the existing row of site name, navigation and theme toggle, which stays exactly as it is. It appears only on the banking pages: the Accounts overview at / and the three valid account detail pages /accounts/everyday, /accounts/savings and /accounts/credit-card. It is hidden on /changelog, on not-found pages (including invalid account ids such as /accounts/mystery), and on every other path. It is fixed text with no sign-out control and no data loading.

constraints.detail: No authentication exists in this repository (lib/accounts.ts, app/accounts/[id]/page.tsx). The strip is a display of the fixed demo identity and must not introduce or imply a session, cookie, token or auth context.

Next.js 16.2.6 / React 19.2.4. AGENTS.md warns this Next.js version has breaking changes; check node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before relying on any routing hook behaviour (usePathname is already used in Header.tsx).
Header is mounted once, in app/layout.tsx, without props. The change must not require layout.tsx to pass anything new.

deferred_decisions: Whether Header imports VALID_ACCOUNT_IDS directly from lib/accounts.ts (which also imports data/accounts.json, pulling the fictional account data into the client bundle) or the engineer extracts the id list into a small data-free module that lib/accounts.ts re-exports. Either is acceptable; it is a bundle-size trade-off the engineer is better placed to judge, provided there remains one source of truth.

The exact strip styling (height, font size, background vs. border treatment) is left to the engineer within the palette and contrast constraints, because the user asked only for 'a thin strip' and the visual check in AC8/AC9 governs the result.
Whether the show/hide rule is a small helper inside Header.tsx or a separate function is left to the engineer; it is internal structure no criterion depends on.

flows.title: Whether the header shows the signed-in strip

must: WHILE the current path is exactly /, /accounts/everyday, /accounts/savings or /accounts/credit-card the system shall show a strip in the site header reading "Signed in as Alex Taylor".

WHILE the current path is anything other than those four paths the system shall not show the signed-in strip, including /changelog, /accounts, any /accounts/<id> whose id is not in VALID_ACCOUNT_IDS (matched case-sensitively), any deeper path such as /accounts/everyday/extra, and any unknown path.
WHEN a visitor moves between a banking page and a non-banking page by client-side navigation the system shall show or hide the strip to match the new path without a full page reload.

The system shall render the strip inside the existing <header> element as its first content, above the row containing the Northline Bank site name, navigation and theme toggle, so the page keeps exactly one banner landmark.
The system shall render the strip as plain text that is not a heading, link or button, and shall not offer any sign-out or log-out control.
The system shall keep the existing header row unchanged: the Northline Bank link to /, the Accounts and Changelog nav links with their active-state accent, and the theme toggle.
The system shall source the strip's text from fixed code with no network, storage or session lookup, and the text shall contain no account number, digits or other customer data beyond the name.

The system shall render the strip's text and background from the existing palette tokens in app/globals.css so that its text meets WCAG 2.1 AA contrast (at least 4.5:1) in both the light and dark themes.
WHILE the viewport is 375px wide the system shall keep the strip to a single line without overlapping or reflowing the header row beneath it.

outcome: Visitors on the Northline Bank sandbox's banking pages see a thin strip at the top of the header saying "Signed in as Alex Taylor".
rationale:
**Why inside the existing header.** The user asked for a strip above the current header. Putting it inside the existing `<header>` (rather than as a sibling in app/layout.tsx) keeps a single banner landmark, so screen readers announce it with the rest of the header, and keeps all header logic in the one client component that already reads the path via `usePathname`. layout.tsx needs no change.

**Why decide by exact path.** Header.tsx already has the current pathname. Showing the strip only for `/` and `/accounts/<id>` where id is in `VALID_ACCOUNT_IDS` hides it on not-found pages without any extra signal from the page, and stays in step if an account is added. A prefix check (`startsWith('/accounts')`) would wrongly show it on `/accounts/mystery`, which the user explicitly did not want (the choice the user delegated was resolved to 'hide it there').

**Wording and no sign-out.** "Signed in as Alex Taylor" is the familiar internet-banking phrasing and does not duplicate the page's "Hello, Alex" greeting. A sign-out link that does nothing would confuse visitors, so there is none.

**Tests.** No Header unit test exists today; a new `__tests__/Header.test.tsx` follows the flat `<Component>.test.tsx` convention and mocks `next/navigation`'s `usePathname` as the changelog tests already do. Every hiding test first renders a banking path and asserts the strip shows, so it cannot pass vacuously against today's header (DTI-01). The inputs are chosen against specific wrong implementations: `/changelog` (shown everywhere), `/accounts/mystery` and `/accounts` (prefix match), `/accounts/EVERYDAY` (case-insensitive match), `/accounts/everyday/extra` (startsWith on a valid id). AC7 is regression coverage by the existing e2e suite and ThemeToggle tests; AC8–AC10 are visual and server-render checks that jsdom cannot decide, so a person checks them (UMC-01).

I read the repository for this: components/Header.tsx, app/layout.tsx, app/page.tsx, app/accounts/[id]/page.tsx, lib/accounts.ts, app/globals.css, components/ThemeToggle.tsx, __tests__/ThemeToggle.test.tsx, jest.setup.ts and e2e/banking.e2e.ts.
